newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Dhaka stocks lose 7 percent following court action.
newsitem.headline: Dhaka stocks lose 7 percent following court action.

text.p: Dhaka stocks plunged more than seven percent at close on Thursday as investors stayed on the sidelines, unnerved by a court order for the arrests of alleged market manipulators, brokers said.
The Dhaka Stock Exchange all-share price index closed 87.46 points or 7.13 percent down at 1,138.46 on a turnover of 43.6 million taka. Of 113 traded issues, 100 lost, 10 gained and 3 were unchanged.
"There were few clients in the market. Investors were anxious and took to the sideline to watch for a while following the overnight developments," said broker M. A. Hossain.
Dhaka's chief metropolitan magistrate court on Wednesday issued arrest warrants for 36 company directors and brokers, including the DSE chairman Imtiyaz Husain.
The arrest orders followed an investigation by the Securities Exchange Commission (SEC) in which the 36 were implicated in alleged fraud in the capital market.
Singer Bangladesh lost 2,812 taka to 5,670, Leasing company IDLC shed 473 to 4261 and Pragati Insurance gained 10 to 745.
